title: Finite unions and proper preimages of closed subsets proper over a base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme; 'proper over $S$' for closed subsets is as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (1) Let $X\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $Z_1,\dots,Z_n\subseteq X$ closed subsets proper over $S$; then $Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_n$ is proper over $S$. (2) Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes locally of finite type over $S$, and $Z\subseteq Y$ a closed subset proper over $S$; then $f^{-1}(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$.

proof.text: For two closed subsets A and B, use the actual constructions i = (vanishingIdeal A).subschemeι and j = (vanishingIdeal B).subschemeι. Their ranges are A and B by Mathlib range_subschemeι and coe_support_vanishingIdeal, and the hypotheses are definitionally IsProper (i ≫ sX) and IsProper (j ≫ sX). The closed immersions are finite, and Mathlib IsFinite.instDescScheme makes g = coprod.desc i j finite and therefore universally closed. No application of the bundled reduced_induced_closed_subscheme theorem is needed.

proof.text: Apply image_isClosedSubsetProperOver_of_universallyClosed to g and the whole closed subset. Mathlib isCompl_range_inl_inr says that the two coprojection ranges cover the coproduct. Together with coprod.inl_desc and coprod.inr_desc and the ranges of i and j, this identifies range g with A union B. Extensionality identifies the resulting closed subset with A supremum B.

proof.text: Induct on n. For n = 0 use properness of bottom and iSup_of_empty. For n + 1, Fin.cases and the universal property of the supremum give the equality iSup Z = Z 0 supremum (iSup (fun i : Fin n => Z i.succ)). Apply the binary union result and the induction hypothesis.

proof.text: For the inverse-image clause let i be the canonical closed immersion of the vanishing-ideal subscheme of Z. The hypothesis gives IsProper (i ≫ sY). Form pullback f i. Its first projection is a closed immersion by base change of i, and its second is proper by base change of f. The equality f ≫ sY = sX and pullback.condition rewrite the first projection composed with sX as the second projection composed with i ≫ sY, hence a proper composite. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_fst (the range corollary of its points description) identifies the first projection range with f inverse-image range i = f inverse-image Z. Apply the existential closed-structure characterization to conclude.

lean.statement: theorem isClosedSubsetProperOver_union_preimage {X S : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] : (∀ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin n → TopologicalSpace.Closeds X), (∀ i, IsClosedSubsetProperOver sX (Z i)) → IsClosedSubsetProperOver sX (⨆ i, Z i)) ∧ (∀ {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (sY : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [IsProper f], f ≫ sY = sX → ∀ (Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds Y), IsClosedSubsetProperOver sY Z → IsClosedSubsetProperOver sX (Z.preimage (f := f.base) f.continuous))
